open_points.subject: owner-session identity format
open_points.text: `random_values` owns minting “the owner session's identity … as a random UUID”, while A13 rule 7 says “The session's identity … [is] at least 32 bytes from the operating system's random source.” A UUID contains only 16 bytes of random identity data.
open_points.question: Is an owner-session identity a UUID, or an opaque value containing at least 32 random bytes?
options: Use the UUID format required by State 1 and `random_values`
Use at least 32 random bytes as required by A13
Define a UUID-based composite carrying at least 32 random bytes
open_points.default_guess: Use an opaque value containing at least 32 random bytes, because it is an authentication bearer.

witness.initial: Registry has no owner session, and the owner signs in successfully.
events: `owner_sessions` asks `random_values` for the new session identity.
`owner_interface` sends that identity in the session cookie.
outcomes: The cookie contains a UUID derived from 16 random bytes.
The cookie contains an opaque encoding of at least 32 random bytes and is not a UUID.
witness.observer: The owner's browser and tests validating the cookie format

open_points.subject: serialization of agent reads against access changes
open_points.text: `store` says only that “a transaction that changes anything takes [the one write lock] when it begins”, while A10 rule 6 requires “A call and every change of its session — a revocation, an archiving, the session's end — [to be] applied one at a time” and decides acceptance by which transaction commits first. `agent_sessions` says the access check is inside the call's transaction, but no module owns serialization of a read-only agent call against those writes.
open_points.question: What module and lock make a read-only agent call atomic and ordered against revocation, archiving and session end?
options: `store` serializes every agent call with those writes
`agent_sessions` owns a separate call/access lock spanning the complete operation
Snapshot ordering is sufficient, with an explicit rule defining which transaction is first
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` serialize the complete agent call transaction with access-changing transactions.

witness.initial: Session S is granted active project P.
events: Cabinet Kernel starts reading P's agent projection for S and passes the session/set check.
Before that read completes, the owner revokes P from S and the revocation commits.
outcomes: Because the read finishes after the revocation, A10 rule 6 makes it observe the changed session and return the not-found refusal.
A read transaction retains its earlier snapshot, so it returns P's projection even though the revocation committed before the read completed.

open_points.subject: contract version in backup metadata
open_points.text: `release_declarations` owns “the release's own version and its contract version, which every audit entry (M09) and every backup's record (A18 rule 1) name”, but A18 rule 1 and the `backups` section enumerate a backup record as only its instant, release, last audit sequence number and key digest.
open_points.question: Must each backup's readable record include the contract version as well as the release version?
options: Include both release and contract versions
Include only the release version, as A18's exhaustive list says
open_points.default_guess: Include only the release version, following A18's explicit backup-record definition.

witness.initial: A running release has release version R and contract version C.
events: The backup's unencrypted record is read.
outcomes: The record contains both R and C, as `release_declarations` says.
The record contains R but no C, as A18 and `backups` say.
witness.observer: The owner or restore tooling reading the backup record

open_points.subject: authentication before transport-value parsing
open_points.text: The check-order rule says stage (1), authentication and the right to the operation, is the first failure, but `service_api` owns “reading the token and the request” and must not own any check, while `operations` owns the check and must not own transport or wire format. No interface permits authentication before `service_api` has decoded a possibly malformed request.
open_points.question: Who orders token authentication ahead of request-body decoding failures without making `service_api` own an authorization check or `operations` own wire parsing?
options: `service_api` identifies the route and asks `operations` to authenticate before decoding the body
`operations` accepts an undecoded request and invokes transport decoding after stage (1)
Transport syntax failures are explicitly outside A04's check order and may precede authentication
open_points.default_guess: Use a two-step operations entry point: authenticate the route and token first, then let `service_api` decode values and continue the operation.

witness.initial: The service API is running on a valid operation route.
events: A caller sends a wrong service token and a malformed request body.
outcomes: Stage (1) runs first and the caller receives the wrong-token refusal without body parsing.
`service_api` parses the body before it can call `operations`, so the caller receives a malformed-request refusal.

open_points.subject: audit sequence verification inside a backup copy
open_points.text: A18 requires the checked decrypted store's never-lowered audit sequence number to equal the backup record's number. `audit_log` owns that counter but exposes it for the live store; only `store` may open the decrypted SQLite copy, and `store` “must not own … the audit log's sequence rule”; `backups` owns the comparison but may not open SQLite. No declared capability crosses the snapshot's counter to `backups`.
open_points.question: Which module reads the audit sequence counter from the snapshot/decrypted backup and supplies it for comparison with the backup record?
options: `store.check_store_file` returns the raw stored counter without owning its semantics
`audit_log` gains a capability to read its counter through a store-file handle supplied by `store`
`backups` is allowed to read this one metadata value from the SQLite copy
open_points.default_guess: Have `store.check_store_file` return the raw counter and let `backups` own the equality check.

open_points.unit: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.subject: diagnostic redaction guarantee
open_points.text: “No module puts a secret … into … a diagnostic” is stated as an obligation on every module, and State 0 also forbids personal values in diagnostics, but no module owns diagnostic construction, redaction or the diagnostic sink. `configuration` and `backups` each emit diagnostics, and parsing/store modules can also encounter caller-supplied personal values.
open_points.question: Which module owns the mechanism that guarantees every diagnostic excludes secrets and personal data?
options: A single diagnostic capability owns construction and redaction
Each diagnostic-producing module owns its own enforcement
Diagnostics are restricted to a closed, value-free vocabulary owned by `models`
open_points.default_guess: Use one value-free diagnostic capability and require producers to pass only declared diagnostic kinds and non-sensitive item names.
